record.original_question: Prove that if Omega is strongly pseudoconvex then there is an absolute constant K > 0 such that the integrated Kobayashi distance between any two points can be realized by a Kobayashi chain of K discs. [For instance, on a convex domain, K = 1.] Prize $50 -S. Krantz. sk @math.wustl.edu

evidence.quote: Prize Problem 1 Prove that if Ω is strongly pseudoconvex then there is an absolute constant K > 0 such that the integrated Kobayashi distance between any two points can be realized by a Kobayashi chain of K discs. [For instance, on a convex domain, K = 1.] Prize $50 -S. Krantz. sk @math.wustl.edu

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a strongly pseudoconvex domain with smooth boundary. Recall the Kobayashi pseudodistance $d_\Omega^K$ on $\Omega$ is defined as follows. For $p, q \in \Omega$, a Kobayashi chain of length $m$ joining $p$ to $q$ is a finite sequence of holomorphic maps $f_1, \dots, f_m : \mathbb{D} \to \Omega$ (where $\mathbb{D}$ is the unit disc in $\mathbb{C}$) together with points $a_i, b_i \in \mathbb{D}$ for $i = 1, \dots, m$, such that $f_1(a_1) = p$, $f_m(b_m) = q$, and $f_i(b_i) = f_{i+1}(a_{i+1})$ for $1 \le i < m$. The Kobayashi distance is
$$d_\Omega^K(p,q) = \inf \sum_{i=1}^m \rho_{\mathbb{D}}(a_i, b_i),$$
where $\rho_{\mathbb{D}}$ is the Poincaré distance on $\mathbb{D}$ and the infimum is taken over all Kobayashi chains joining $p$ to $q$. The integrated Kobayashi distance is the length distance associated with the infinitesimal Kobayashi metric, which coincides with $d_\Omega^K$ on domains where they agree.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $K > 0$ (independent of $\Omega$ and of the points) such that for every strongly pseudoconvex domain $\Omega$ and every pair of points $p, q \in \Omega$, the value $d_\Omega^K(p,q)$ is realized (or attained as the infimum) by a Kobayashi chain consisting of at most $K$ analytic discs. (For comparison, on a convex domain one may take $K = 1$.)
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this question. There has been substantial progress on local extremal discs near strongly pseudoconvex boundary points (Lempert, Burns–Krantz) and on sharp estimates for the Kobayashi distance on strongly pseudoconvex domains, as well as visibility-type results, but no source explicitly states that the chain-length problem with a uniform constant $K$ has been settled affirmatively or negatively. Status appears unverified.

status_evidence.title: Precise estimates of invariant distances on strongly pseudoconvex domains
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp estimates for the Kobayashi distance, the Lempert function, and the Carathéodory distance on strongly pseudoconvex domains with C^{2,α}-smooth boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Active research provides sharp estimates but does not resolve the uniform-chain-length question.

status_evidence.title: Pseudoconvexity, Analytic Discs, and Invariant Metrics — S. G. Krantz
status_evidence.snippet: Burns and Krantz constructed a local theory of extremal discs near a strongly pseudoconvex boundary point.
status_evidence.claim: Only a local theory of extremal discs is established; global uniform bound on chain length is not asserted to be proved.
